title: Shifted determinant evaluation for a finite locally free sheaf
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let M be a sheaf of O_X-modules, and let d≥0 be an integer. Assume M is finite locally free of constant rank d [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Let M^dual=Hom_{O_X}(M,O_X) be its internal sheaf dual. In the derived category [def-pc-derived-category] with its recorded K-flat tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], the objects (\bigwedge^d M^dual)[-d] and (\bigwedge^d M)[d] have tensor product isomorphic to the derived unit O_X[0]. Here a sheaf inside the derived category means its single complex in degree zero and the exterior powers are sheafified sectionwise exterior powers [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power].

source.place: Tag 0BRT (lemma-smooth-proper), final paragraph: determinant of the normal sheaf is invertible with inverse the conormal determinant

proof.text: Apply determinant_dual_evaluation to M and hfree. This gives an ordinary sheaf tensor isomorphism L tensor F ≅ O_X for the two top exterior sheaves.

Install the recorded sheaf monoidal, symmetric, closed and Grothendieck structures and its functorial flat resolution. The existing ObjectProperty.flat_of_tensorIso proves L flat directly from its tensor inverse. The single complex of L is K-flat by CochainComplex.kFlat_single_obj_iff_flat, and quotient preserves K-flatness. DerivedMonoidal.isIso_counit_app_app_of_kFlat_left makes the Qh tensor comparison invertible. Compose it with the quotient monoidal comparison and the tensor-of-single-complex comparison to identify S(L) tensor S(F) with S(L tensor F). Map the ordinary determinant isomorphism through S, and use DerivedCategory.isIso_ε_Qh to identify S(O_X) with the derived unit. These compositions are the proved private singleObjIsoQh, singleObjTensorIso and singleObjUnitIso helpers.

For arbitrary derived A and B, choose K-flat representatives of A and B[b] using DerivedCategory.exists_kFlat_iso. The existing commShiftTensorLeftQhObj and commShiftTensorRightQhObj give one-variable shift commutation on these representatives. Transport along their isomorphisms by Functor.CommShift.ofIso. Compose the first-variable comparison, the shift of the second-variable comparison and shiftFunctorAdd to obtain A[a] tensor B[b] ≅ (A tensor B)[a+b]. This is the fully proved private tensorShiftIso helper; it does not identify the independent universes u and w. Apply it at a=-d, b=d, map the derived unshifted evaluation through shift zero, and compose shiftFunctorZero. neg_add_cancel proves the required shift equality.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BRT final determinant inversion; ordinary evaluation split off, K-flat localization and shift composition formalized by P3 using upstream Etale.Derived.Invertible and DerivedCategory.Monoidal.Shift

Mathlib results are unrelated uses of dualizing; direct source search finds exteriorPower.pairingDual in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/ExteriorPower/Pairing.lean. It is a ring-module pairing, not a shifted derived sheaf isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem shiftedDeterminant_dual_evaluation (X : Scheme.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] (M : X.Modules) (d : ℕ) (hfree : M.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank d) : Nonempty ((((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj (Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf) M (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)) d))⟦-(d : ℤ)⟧ ⊗ ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj (Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf M d))⟦(d : ℤ)⟧) ≅ 𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory X))
